title: How do you draw a square from its diagonal, with no protractor?
description: A square with a diagonal of six centimetres has to be drawn with a ruler and compass only. The video makes the right angle through the midpoint with arcs, marks the other two corners, and checks the diagonals and sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: arcs from the two ends of the diagonal give a line at right angles through its midpoint, and the other corners lie on it at the same distance from the midpoint. Watch for students who draw the arcs with too small an opening.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 6)
video_script.why: The child draws a square from its diagonal as before, but makes the right angle through the midpoint with arcs and a ruler, with no protractor.
video_script.substitution: Draw the diagonal, make the line at right angles through its midpoint with two pairs of arcs, mark the other two corners at the same distance, and join the four corners.
video_script.anchor: diagonal AB of 6 cm with arcs from A and B crossing above and below it, and a line through the crossings
video_script.payoff_line: Eigh C B D is the square, with both diagonals six centimetres

final_answer.value: ACBD is the square, with diagonals AB = CD = 6 cm
final_answer.spoken: eigh C B D is the square, with both diagonals six centimetres

maths_rules: AB = 6 cm; arcs with the same opening, more than 3 cm, from A and from B on both sides of AB cross in two places; the line through them is perpendicular to AB through its midpoint O
OA = OB = 3 cm; with centre O and opening 3 cm, mark C and D on this line on opposite sides of AB, so OC = OD = 3 cm and CD = 6 cm
join A, C, B, D in order
the diagonals AB = CD = 6 cm are equal, bisect each other and meet at 90 degrees, so the figure is a square
check: the four sides measure the same with a ruler and each corner fits a set square
video_script.design: One idea: the arcs give the right angle at the midpoint, with no protractor. The diagonal and the crossing line stay on the board.
